documents.title: Complete AI Guidelines
documents.summary: Provost guidelines for the whole community covering principles, data protection, verification and disclosure, then separate sections for students, instructors, researchers and administrative staff. For students, AI is banned on assignments and exams unless the syllabus grants permission.
documents.stance_why: The student section says 'Unless an instructor includes a clear statement in their syllabus granting permission, the use of generative AI tools to complete an assignment or exam is prohibited', which is a ban unless permitted. Instructors set the permissions, but the university sets this default, so restrict rather than delegates.

units.why: "Usage of AI tools in academic work, research, or administrative activities must be clearly disclosed" requires disclosure of AI use; P24 is the disclosure type and the actor is the whole community.

documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy
documents.summary: A general academic integrity policy and adjudication process in which AI appears in the definitions of cheating and plagiarism and in the faculty duty to put an AI statement on syllabi. Most of the text is procedure for all incidents, and a few units are coded because they apply to AI cases.
documents.stance_why: Cheating covers AI 'not authorized by the instructor' and plagiarism covers AI-produced work 'without proper citation', so AI is barred unless authorized or cited, which is restrict.

units.fit_note: Frames acknowledgment of AI sources as a general integrity responsibility rather than a per-submission disclosure.
